claims.statement: The gateway dispatches plain and materialized CREATE VIEW forms to the same handler; both compile and populate when shard-backed, while materialized creation additionally tracks backfill and bound-source ingestion.

Gateway view dependency expansion recursively substitutes catalog SQL into FROM/JOIN subqueries with a depth budget of 16; compilation requires base-table dependencies while the catalog retains original dependency names.

Local view compilation failure returns RS-1019 before catalog registration without a legacy materializer fallback; standalone gateways register without local compilation, while distributed creation deploys supported aggregate or aggregate-over-equi-join plans.
View creation checks duplicate handling, dependency cycles and workload existence before registering SQL, columns, sink operator ID and dependency mutations in CatalogStubs.
ViewSink persists signed output keyed by operator ID, epoch and row index, and a separate view directory maps view names to operator ID, column count and primary key for independent shard readers.

Initial compiled-view population scans existing source data once, scanning both join inputs when needed, then persists output and arrangements; normal incremental refresh processes signed row deltas instead of rescanning tables.

Gateway view DDL is not an atomic catalog-directory-backfill transaction: CatalogStubs ignores durable commit errors and may spawn persistence, while directory write failure only warns and can leave published reads without rows.

Generic bound-source backfill recovers an owner-leased runtime, reuses or captures a snapshot/delta fence, persists intent and resumes from durable phase/cursor before bounded snapshot and catch-up processing.

Accepted source backfill commits put input, output, operator state, checkpoint, cursor, lifecycle and frontier in one M3 write; catch-up enforces a byte limit with RS-4020 and commits a Running publication epoch before catalog publication.
Materialized backfill projects snapshotting and catching-up phases before Running; post-registration failures can return RS-4022 and leave a defined unpublished view whose reads are rejected.

Pgoutput coordination is source-scoped using host, port, database, slot, publication, authentication principal and credential reference; durable physical-slot bindings reject competing identities and shared aliases must use the same shard.

A new pgoutput coordinator commits a source-wide snapshot as an envelope at its snapshot LSN; additional view attachment initializes from local imported tables under coordinator and shard locks at the committed source offset.

Shared-trace AttachedView installation separately loads a pinned snapshot, registers a consumer frontier and drains deltas above the pin, with bounded buffering returning RS-4020; ViewRefOp separately tails upstream sink epoch deltas rather than defining gateway SQL expansion semantics.

Gateway update reachability expands through original catalog dependencies and orders executable views topologically; pgoutput envelopes feed downstream output deltas and append affected view state/output to the transaction batch.

SQL SchemaCatalog persists SQL, plan and output schema in versioned entries, accepts replacement only when the existing ordered name/type prefix is unchanged, increments accepted versions, and rejects incompatible changes with RS-1002 before replacement writes; its classifier does not enforce nullable appended columns.

Pgoutput route compatibility preserves relation/imported-table and replica identity plus existing column-name/key prefix, allows nullable or defaulted appendages and supported lossless widening, and rejects drops, renames/reorders, key identity changes and narrowing.

Generic schema evolution descriptors classify nullable additions, type-tag widening and merge-law compatibility and model clone/backfill/flip; this is separate from gateway OR REPLACE, which uses the gateway creation path rather than SchemaCatalog registration or automatic downstream recompilation.

Pgoutput relation staging routes namespace/name to source aliases and imported tables, stages unrelated relations as unrouted and blocks unsupported or incompatible metadata instead of reinterpreting data.

Pgoutput transaction commits validate row schema versions against routes and combine imported rows, affected output/state, routes/history, frontier, lifecycles and source offset via commit_replayable_epoch, updating catalog column projections afterward.

Breaking pgoutput relation changes durably record RS-1002 with xid, metadata and last-safe LSN before blocking; failure handling restores persisted pipeline state and closes ownership, and durable blocked state prevents ordinary resume/restart from bypassing the shared-source block.

Compiled-view recovery reconstructs process-local pipelines from catalog SQL using the durable sink ID and deterministic stage IDs, restores arrangements, and uses durable source lifecycles to restart workers or continue backfill.

Current recover_compiled_views warns and continues on arrangement restoration failures and logs recompilation failures without installing live refresh; compiled-plan identity tests separately verify seven identity fields, version/dependency rejection and a directly driven LifecycleTracker readiness model rather than end-to-end fatal recovery.
ViewState exposes paused, running, backfilling and over-budget states, but CLI pause/resume delegates to CatalogApi and the remote implementation currently rejects these view mutations with RS-0004.

Gateway source pause changes status and shared pgoutput ownership closes when no active aliases remain; resume sets OK and can spawn a dependent pgoutput worker, so pausing one alias is not necessarily pausing the shared slot.

Gateway view drop removes catalog and compiled-cache entries without itself deleting output/directory keys or dropping an upstream slot; PostgreSQL CDC source drop rejects dependent views and attempts coordinator cleanup only after the last alias is removed.
Running PostgreSQL source identity option changes are rejected with RS-4013 and require pause, drain and explicit rebinding instead of a live identity switch.

The schema evolution cookbook recommends in-place compatible changes and new-view or source migration for breaking changes; focused pgoutput tests verify route history for nullable/defaulted additions and widening and classify breaking changes.
